title: Using Too and Enough
summary: Learn how to use too and enough to talk about amounts and limits. You will practice describing when something is more or less than you need.

sections.p: We use the word 'too' before adjectives and adverbs to mean 'more than we want or need'. It has a negative feeling because something is a problem. For example, if the coffee is too hot, you cannot drink it right now. It is extra and causes trouble.

ex.en: This jacket is too small for me.
ex.mean: The jacket is smaller than the size I need.

ex.en: The music is too loud in this room.
ex.mean: There is more sound than I want to hear.

ex.en: He drove too fast on the wet road.
ex.mean: His speed was higher than was safe.

sections.p: We use 'enough' after adjectives and adverbs to mean 'as much as we need'. It usually has a positive feeling. Notice the word order: adjective first, then 'enough'. If something is warm enough, it is good.

ex.en: Are you warm enough in that coat?
ex.mean: Do you have the right amount of warmth?

ex.en: This room is big enough for our meeting.
She didn't run fast enough to win the race.
ex.mean: Her speed was lower than the required amount.

sections.p: We also use 'enough' with nouns to mean the correct amount. But remember the word order is different here! 'Enough' comes before the noun. You can say 'enough money' or 'enough time'.

ex.en: I have enough money to buy lunch.
ex.mean: I possess the correct amount of money.

ex.en: We don't have enough time for this game.
ex.mean: We lack the required amount of time.

ex.en: Do you have enough chairs for everyone?
ex.mean: Is the number of chairs sufficient?

tip: Remember: 'Too' goes BEFORE adjectives (too hot), but 'enough' goes AFTER adjectives (hot enough) and BEFORE nouns (enough water).

quiz.en: Put on a sweater. It is ___ cold outside today.
I can't buy this phone. It is not cheap ___.
We have ___ food for all our guests.
Please turn down the TV. It is ___ loud!
Can we go home now? I am tired ___.
He made mistakes because he worked ___ quickly.
